title: Optimal detuning and gate time for strongly driven single-qubit gates beyond the rotating-wave approximation
authors: Alejandro D. Bendersky, Sergio S. Gomez, Rodolfo H. Romero
abstract: Single-qubit quantum gates are implemented as the time-controlled unitary evolution of a two-level system under harmonic driving. The rotating-wave approximation (RWA) provides closed-form gate parameters for weak coupling. Larger amplitudes, desirable to speed up the dynamics, make the RWA-designed gates inaccurate because of the neglected counter-rotating term, which also shifts the resonance (Bloch-Siegert shift). Here we study theoretically the infidelity of gates beyond the RWA, using the effective Magnus-Taylor Hamiltonian through second order in the inverse of the driving frequency. By detuning the driving frequency by an amplitude-dependent shift of Bloch-Siegert type and rescaling the operation time, the RWA gate conditions are recovered with corrected parameters. Numerical solutions of the Schrodinger equation show that these corrections lower the gate infidelity by several orders of magnitude, extending the range of usable amplitudes
summary: This theoretical paper improves the design of single-qubit quantum gates by correcting the limitations of the Rotating-Wave Approximation (RWA) under strong driving. Using the Magnus-Taylor expansion, the authors derive optimal detuning and time rescaling parameters. These corrections drastically lower gate infidelity, allowing for the reliable operation of gates at much higher driving amplitudes than previously thought possible.
main_problem: The paper addresses the inaccuracy of single-qubit quantum gates designed using the Rotating-Wave Approximation (RWA) when strong driving fields are employed.
main_result: By applying corrections derived from the effective Magnus-Taylor Hamiltonian, the gate infidelity can be reduced by several orders of magnitude, significantly extending the usable range of driving amplitudes.
method: The authors use the Magnus-Taylor expansion up to second order in the inverse of the driving frequency to derive an effective, time-independent Hamiltonian that accounts for neglected counter-rotating terms.
model_or_system: The system is a two-level atom or qubit driven by a time-harmonic field, modeled by a Hamiltonian $H_{BS}(t) = \omega_0/2 \sigma_z + A \sin(\omega t)\sigma_x$.
key_observables: Gate infidelity ($I$), fidelity ($F$), and the effective Hamiltonian parameters ($\Omega, 	heta, \phi$).
important_parameters: The ratio $\lambda = A/\omega$ (amplitude to frequency) and the detuning $\Delta = \omega_0 - \omega$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the perturbative Magnus-Taylor expansion up to second order in $1/\omega$, and the optimal conditions are found for stroboscopic gate measurements.
figures_summary: Figures show the infidelity of Z and H gates versus the ratio $A/\omega$, demonstrating the power-law growth of error beyond RWA, and illustrate the optimal detuning and time corrections.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the failure of RWA at strong driving, then derives the effective Hamiltonian using the Magnus-Taylor expansion, and finally calculates the corrected gate parameters and resulting low-infidelity protocols for Z and H gates.
why_interesting: This work provides concrete, quantitative methods for designing high-fidelity quantum gates in realistic, strongly driven physical systems, which is crucial for scaling up quantum computation.
